headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist because kotaemon ingests sensitive documents and API keys while awesome-prompts can supply untrusted prompt content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt repository, so its outputs can be attacker-controlled instructions. kotaemon processes documents and chat transcripts via a web UI and can ingest content into LLM workflows, creating a plausible injection bridge if prompts or copied text are fed into it. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation controls in the profiles.
conditions: IF content from awesome-prompts is pasted into kotaemon chat or document inputs
IF kotaemon treats imported text as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict imported prompts to a reviewed allowlist
Add a visible provenance banner for copied prompt text
Use a separate workspace for prompt testing
Disable automatic execution of pasted instructions
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches documents, chat transcripts, and API keys and sends requests to external model APIs by default; awesome-prompts is a public prompt source that can steer users toward placing sensitive material into those flows. Even though awesome-prompts has no network egress, the pair can still expose sensitive data through kotaemon's outbound API calls and file-backed workspace.
conditions: IF sensitive documents or API keys are loaded into kotaemon
IF kotaemon routes those inputs to OpenAI, AzureOpenAI, Cohere, Groq, or similar APIs
mitigations: Do not load secrets into the shared workspace
Use a local-only backend such as Ollama or llama-cpp-python
Rotate any API keys already exposed in test data
Limit uploads to non-sensitive sample documents
requires-engineering: enforce redaction before outbound API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts itself has no write surfaces, but kotaemon writes to ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances, so concurrent use can conflict over shared mutable state. The pair is not directly conflicting on filesystem writes, yet kotaemon's shared app data plus repeated prompt experimentation creates a realistic overwrite/corruption risk.
conditions: IF multiple kotaemon instances share the same ./ktem_app_data directory
IF prompt experiments modify shared configuration or cached artifacts
mitigations: Run only one kotaemon instance per data directory
Back up ./ktem_app_data before testing
Use separate per-user workspaces
Check for stale locks before editing shared files
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply persuasive but unverified prompt content, and kotaemon is a support/RAG system that may render or act on retrieved text. If kotaemon treats imported prompts or retrieved snippets as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect answers or actions. The profiles do not show verification gates, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses prompt content from awesome-prompts as authoritative system guidance
IF downstream support responses are generated without human verification
mitigations: Require human review for prompt templates before use
Mark imported prompts as untrusted
Compare outputs against a second source
Log source provenance alongside generated answers
requires-engineering: add verification and citation checks

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles documents, chat transcripts, and API keys, which can trigger retention and residency obligations; awesome-prompts is a public open-source prompt list and is not itself the compliance-sensitive component. The risk arises when sensitive customer data is processed through kotaemon's external API integrations without a documented retention or residency control in the profiles.
conditions: IF customer documents or chat transcripts include regulated personal data
IF those data are sent to third-party model APIs or retained in ./ktem_app_data
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in test runs
Review retention settings in kotaemon
Store data in a region-approved environment
Delete temporary files after each session
requires-engineering: implement residency and deletion controls
